description: The clocked, cross-node share regime (peer PLAN Step 8): the invite→accept→(ratify)→close lifecycle of contracts/share-protocol.md, implemented once in peer-node/services/sparknet-share-regime.py and proven in-process by peer-node/tests/test_share_regime.py. The engine reads the machine contracts (capabilities.json share_types + share_clocks, overlay.json governance_mode + data-plane stanza, ports.json share ports) and refuses to run if they are missing, so it cannot silently drift from the contract. The bridge's /session/:id/share verbs delegate to it, so there is no second copy of the rules.
status: live on the peer_pair; 4203 not bound

engine.governance_source: contracts/overlay.json governance_mode (solo=1, peer_pair=2, master_governed=3+); recomputed on every share request, never cached
engine.clock_source: contracts/capabilities.json share_clocks; contract defaults (invite 1h, idle 20m, ratification 2h, absolute 10h) are what a deployment runs, and tests inject the four clocks in seconds

narrowing: a receiver may accept a narrower type than offered, never a wider one (capabilities.json share_types.narrowing_only); only 'full' carries the explicit includes set

clocks.invite_acceptance: 1h — a recipient may accept within the window
clocks.idle_close: 20m — a *temporary* share closes on inactivity; a permanent share is not idle-closed
clocks.ratification: 2h — master_governed only; silence is a refusal, never an 'awaiting ratification' state
clocks.share_absolute: 10h — a hard cap for both roles; every share, permanent included, ends here

trust: an accepted peer arrives flagged; in master_governed a Master ratification moves it to authenticated and *retains* the flag (capabilities.json trust_levels.retained_after_ratification); in peer_pair both endpoints stay flagged because nothing arbitrates

department_boundary.attestation: the department compared is the `department` field of each node's Master-signed registry entry (contracts/registry-schema.json signed_envelope_fields). It is never read from anything a node says about itself: in-department sharing is the easier path, so a self-declared department would be the cheap way into whichever department a node wanted to read.
department_boundary.binds_when: both sides carry an attested department AND the two differ. Where the Master attested none there is no boundary to cross, so a fresh deployment shares exactly as it did before this rule existed instead of needing a grant nobody has issued yet.
department_boundary.checked_by: both sides, each against its own view of the registry. The offerer is refused at offer(); the acceptor is refused at accept(). Trusting the sender would let one granted node pull an ungranted one across the boundary.
department_boundary.refusal: 403 cross-department, naming the capability that would permit it
department_boundary.narrowing_does_not_help: a narrower share type still needs the capability. The type says what a share conveys; the department says who may share at all, so letting kb-view through because it copies nothing would make the boundary depend on the least sensitive choice available.
department_boundary.audit: an inbound offer a node will refuse is still recorded, with the boundary marked and `permitted_by` null. An attempt refused silently leaves no evidence it was made, and the evidence is the point.
department_boundary.widens_nothing_else: the holder still needs the ordinary share grant, still obeys the four clocks, and in master_governed mode still needs ratification

actions.stanza-up: the acceptor's host may bring up the time-boxed data-plane stanza
actions.teardown-stanza: on explicit close, idle, absolute expiry, or refusal
actions.isolate-data-plane: on non-ratification: the fabric data plane is severed while the authority-and-evidence channel to the Master stays open
actions.re-evaluate: a third node joining mid-share re-evaluates the live share instead of grandfathering it; the share is closed reason re_evaluated and may be re-offered under the new mode

authority_boundary.authority_plane_invariant: a peer's [Peer] AllowedIPs stays exactly 10.100.0.1/32 (contracts/overlay.json peer_allowed_ips_rule); the share stanza is time-boxed data-plane only and never widens it
authority_boundary.structural: the engine opens no sockets, loads no keys and holds no key material; a share is never an authority transfer
authority_boundary.ports: 4201/4202 are live on the peer_pair behind signed transport and a 0600 Unix control socket; 4203 is built and rehearsed on loopback but no unit is enabled. A peer still cannot ratify: only the Master key signs the closed ratification envelope, and the 2 h clock is enforced locally.
